questions.prompt: The mother, forgetting her own fear, hurled herself into the flames.
questions.answer: Māter, suī timōris oblīta, in flammās sē iēcit.

questions.prompt: You will remember us when the harvest has been gathered.
questions.answer: Nostrī meminerīs cum messis collēcta erit.

questions.prompt: The poet remembers many things about the ancient war.
questions.answer: Poēta multa dē bellō antīquō meminit.

questions.prompt: We must not forget Epicurus, whose teaching still endures.
questions.answer: Epicūrī oblīvīscī nōn dēbēmus, cuius doctrīna adhūc manet.

questions.prompt: Forget your anger and remember me, brave king.
questions.answer: Īrae tuae oblīvīscere et meī meminerīs, rēx fortis.

questions.prompt: Remember the disaster, citizens, and guard the walls diligently.
questions.answer: Incommodī reminīsciminī, cīvēs, et mūrōs dīligenter custōdīte.

questions.prompt: The exiles remembered their homeland with tears in their eyes.
questions.answer: Exsulēs patriae meminērunt lacrimīs in oculīs.

questions.prompt: Having forgotten the danger, the boy climbed the highest tree.
questions.answer: Perīculī oblītus, puer arborem altissimam ascendit.

questions.prompt: I remember this clearly, though many years have passed.
questions.answer: Haec clārē meminī, quamquam multī annī praeteriērunt.

questions.prompt: May you never forget the kindness of your teacher.
questions.answer: Benignitātis praeceptōris tuī numquam oblīvīscāris.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, remembering their oath, stood firm in the battle.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, sacrāmentī reminīscentēs, in proeliō cōnstitērunt.

questions.prompt: Remember us when you reach the golden temple of the gods.
questions.answer: Nostrī reminīscere cum ad aureum deōrum templum pervēnerīs.

questions.prompt: Do you not remember the many gifts I once gave you?
questions.answer: Nōnne multa dōna quae ōlim tibi dedī meministī?

questions.prompt: Forgetful of the storm, the sailors set sail at first light.
questions.answer: Tempestātis oblītī, nāvigantēs prīmā lūce vēla dedērunt.

questions.prompt: Let the victors remember the vanquished with mercy.
questions.answer: Victōrēs victōs misericordiā meminerint.

questions.prompt: The queen could not forget the letter sealed with royal wax.
questions.answer: Rēgīna epistolae rēgiā cērā signātae oblīvīscī nōn potuit.

questions.prompt: May you remember us, kindly gods, in this hour of great necessity.
questions.answer: Nostrī meminerītis, dī benignī, hōc magnae necessitātis tempore.

questions.prompt: The poet could not forget the sweetness of his mother's voice.
questions.answer: Poēta suāvitātis māternae vōcis oblīvīscī nōn poterat.

questions.prompt: When you read this tragedy, remember the tears of the conquered.
questions.answer: Cum hanc tragoediam legēs, victōrum lacrimārum mementō.

questions.prompt: I recall many things, but I have forgotten the enemy's name.
questions.answer: Multa meminī, sed hostīlis nōminis oblītus sum.

questions.prompt: Forgetful of the danger, the boy climbed the nearest mulberry tree.
questions.answer: Perīculī oblītus, puer proximam morum ascendit.

questions.prompt: Let us remember our ancestors, whose courage transformed the whole world.
questions.answer: Māiōrum meminerīmus, quōrum virtūs ūniversum orbem immūtāvit.

questions.prompt: The general, remembering the former disaster, feared a new war.
questions.answer: Dux, veteris incommodī reminīscēns, novum bellum timēbat.
